metadata.research_goal: Create a backend-ready level-based teaching draft for association football/soccer that integrates Wave 1 technical, tactical, role, rule, goalkeeping, and performance drafts with official coaching resources and peer-reviewed evidence. The draft defines beginner, intermediate, and advanced expectations, prerequisites, drills, avoid-until-ready gates, assessment signals, position-specific progressions, and transition rules for ball mastery, receiving, passing, dribbling and 1v1, finishing, chance creation, defending and pressing, match IQ, goalkeeping, and football strength and conditioning.

key_concepts.concept: A player can be advanced in one football domain and beginner in another.
key_concepts.backend_use: Unlock progressions by domain evidence rather than by a single global label.
examples: a fast winger may be advanced in 1v1 but beginner in defensive recovery body shape
a goalkeeper may be advanced in shot stopping but intermediate in build-up distribution

key_concepts.concept: Football skill is not only technical execution; it depends on scanning, pressure, space, timing, and the next action.
key_concepts.backend_use: Prefer representative drills once basic movement safety is present.

key_concepts.concept: Close control, surface variety, two-footed touches, change of pace, and ball protection create the base for receiving, dribbling, passing, and finishing.
key_concepts.backend_use: Beginner plans should include frequent ball contacts without over-specializing by position.

key_concepts.concept: Receiving should set up the next action: protect, turn, pass forward, combine, carry, finish, or reset.
key_concepts.backend_use: Assess first touch by next-action quality, not by whether the ball merely stops.

key_concepts.concept: A skill demonstrated in a cone drill is not yet game-ready until it survives opponent pressure, direction, transition, and fatigue.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use unopposed, semi-opposed, opposed, and game-transfer stages inside each level.

key_concepts.concept: Advanced actions must improve football outcomes relative to their risk: line-breaking pass, dribble, shot, cross, press, or goalkeeper distribution.
key_concepts.backend_use: Record error cost and tactical return in assessments.

key_concepts.concept: Beginners need broad football literacy; intermediate players add position priorities; advanced players train role, system, opponent, and match-state details.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not let early specialization remove emergency skills.

key_concepts.concept: Offside, goalkeeper restrictions, foul/card law, heading guidance, and tackle safety constrain what should be taught and when.
key_concepts.backend_use: Attach IFAB and safety gates to advanced defending, finishing, set-piece, and goalkeeper tasks.

key_concepts.concept: Football understanding moves from knowing rules and simple principles to reading phases, exploiting space, managing risk, and adapting to opponents.
key_concepts.backend_use: Assess tactical reasoning in small-sided and 11v11 contexts.

key_concepts.concept: S&C should support repeated high-quality football actions: sprint, decelerate, duel, jump, kick, change direction, recover, and make decisions under fatigue.
key_concepts.backend_use: Avoid conditioning that degrades technical learning or spikes injury risk.

technical_models.model: Progress from confidence and surface variety to pressured manipulation, disguise, and game-transfer control.

technical_models.model: Progress from controlling the ball to receiving with body orientation, scan information, pressure management, and next-action intent.

level_path.beginner: two-touch control and pass to large target
level_path.intermediate: receive across body, safe foot, back-foot/front-foot choices under pressure

level_path.intermediate: target-foot passing, rondos, wall pass, through pass, lofted or driven pass introduction
level_path.advanced: third-player play, switch of play, disguised pass, tempo control, pressure-specific risk choices

technical_models.model: Progress from close control to recognizing when to beat, carry, shield, combine, or release.

level_path.beginner: control and simple moves against passive pressure
level_path.intermediate: isolate defender, change pace, attack space, protect ball, finish or pass after move
level_path.advanced: role-specific 1v1, overload manipulation, contact balance, end-product efficiency

technical_models.model: Progress from contact quality to shot selection, goalkeeper manipulation, first-time finishing, movement, and rebound behavior.

level_path.intermediate: finishing after movement, varied angles, both feet, live goalkeeper cues
level_path.advanced: one-touch, high-speed, pressure finishing, shot value, disguise, rebounds, and match-state choices

technical_models.model: Progress from delivery mechanics to scanning, target-zone selection, runner timing, cutbacks, second balls, and transition defense.

level_path.beginner: deliver from wide channel to large area and attack front/middle/back spaces
level_path.intermediate: low cross, driven cross, cutback, early cross, late runner timing
level_path.advanced: opponent-specific box occupation, disguise, weak-side occupation, rest-defense connection

technical_models.model: Progress from individual stance and delay to unit pressing, compactness, counterpressing, and lawful duel behavior.

level_path.beginner: goal-side, slow down, jockey, force away from goal, safe tackling rules
level_path.intermediate: pressure-cover-balance, intercept, screen lanes, coordinated pressing triggers
level_path.advanced: team press, mid/low block, rest-defense response, trap design, transition decisions

technical_models.model: Progress from rules and simple principles to phase recognition, formation roles, game-state management, scouting, and KPI interpretation.

level_path.beginner: rules, zones, support, width/depth, compact defending
level_path.intermediate: formations, phase roles, pressing cues, overloads, transition choices
level_path.advanced: scout plan, opponent adjustment, rotation-specific roles, set-piece and game-state management

level_path.beginner: ready position, catch, scoop, basic dive shape, roll/pass distribution
level_path.intermediate: set timing, angle, 1v1, cross decision, driven distribution, communication
level_path.advanced: sweeper-keeper, pressure build-up, high claims, rebound control, defensive organization

technical_models.model: Progress from movement competency and injury-prevention habits to role-specific speed, repeatability, strength, power, and in-season load management.

level_path.beginner: warm-up habits, landing, sprint mechanics, basic strength, mobility, low fatigue
level_path.intermediate: acceleration, deceleration, change of direction, repeated sprint exposure, unilateral strength
level_path.advanced: position-specific high-speed exposure, microcycle planning, return-to-play staging, load monitoring

tactical_rules.rule: Receiver should scan before ball arrival when time and safety allow, then choose body shape and first touch from pressure and space.

level_emphasis.intermediate: check shoulder before receiving and play away from pressure
level_emphasis.advanced: scan multiple times, disguise, and act before pressure closes

tactical_rules.rule: First touch should prepare the intended next action rather than simply stopping the ball.
Prefer forward progression when body shape, pressure, and support make it secure; reset when progression risk is higher than reward.
In 1v1 and overload situations, commit a defender before passing, crossing, or cutting back when this creates a better chance.
Finishing decisions should account for distance, angle, pressure, goalkeeper position, passing options, rebound space, and game state.
When the byline or half-space entry allows it, scan for cutback and low driven options before serving a blind aerial cross.
The nearest defender pressures, the next player covers, and the unit balances central or goal-side risk.
Press when a cue appears and support is connected: poor touch, backwards pass, receiver facing own goal, pass into trap, or isolated wide receiver.
After losing the ball, counterpress only if nearby players can close ball, lanes, and forward options; otherwise recover behind the ball.
Attacking practice should include protection against counterattack through staggered cover, central security, and recovery roles.
Goalkeeper distribution should match pressure, available support, score context, and team build-up ability.
Defensive duels must be taught through IFAB law constraints: control, timing, no excessive force, and no reckless follow-through.

physical_demands.demand: Repeated short accelerations and reaccelerations after a touch, tackle, press, or transition.
physical_demands.level_implication: Introduce mechanics and low-volume starts at beginner level; progress to reactive and position-specific doses.

physical_demands.demand: Wide players, forwards, fullbacks, center backs defending space, and transition moments require high-speed exposure.
physical_demands.level_implication: Avoid sudden sprint spikes; advanced players need planned exposure in the weekly cycle.

physical_demands.demand: Pressing, dribbling, defending, shooting preparation, and receiving turns all require braking and cutting.
physical_demands.level_implication: Teach braking alignment before repeated max-effort change-of-direction work.

physical_demands.demand: Kicking, shielding, landing, cutting, and contact duels are often single-leg or asymmetrical.
physical_demands.level_implication: Progress from balance and split-squat patterns to loaded and reactive single-leg strength.

physical_demands.demand: Passing, shooting, aerial control, shielding, and duels require trunk stiffness and hip rotation control.
physical_demands.level_implication: Develop through basic bracing and rotation control before high-volume kicking and contact drills.

physical_demands.demand: Heading, goalkeeping claims, set pieces, and aerial duels involve jumping, landing, and contact.
physical_demands.level_implication: Use age and heading guidance, landing quality, and collision management as progression gates.

physical_demands.demand: Long passing, shooting, crossing, clearances, and goalkeeper distribution create hip flexor, adductor, quad, and trunk load.
physical_demands.level_implication: Track spikes in high-force kicking, especially when adding long-range, weak-foot, or fatigued finishing work.

physical_demands.demand: Goalkeepers need lateral pushes, dives, low saves, high claims, recoveries, and landing tolerance.
physical_demands.level_implication: Build save technique and fall tolerance before high-volume power service.

physical_demands.demand: Players need the capacity to repeat technical and tactical actions across match duration.
physical_demands.level_implication: Use football-specific games and intervals without removing technical quality from key sessions.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Rapid increases in sprinting, high-speed running, or fatigued pressing can raise hamstring risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Progress sprint exposure, include posterior-chain strength, and monitor next-day response.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High kicking volume, cutting, slide tackles, and lateral defending load the adductor and groin complex.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Progress kicking and COD volume; use strength and symptom monitoring before advanced loads.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Tackles, landing on another foot, uneven surfaces, and rapid cuts can overload ankle and foot structures.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Train landing, balance, footwear-surface awareness, and reduce uncontrolled duel volume.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High-speed cutting, pressing deceleration, awkward landings, and contact duels can increase knee risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use neuromuscular warm-up, landing mechanics, hip-knee-ankle control, and fatigue gates.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Heading and aerial challenges can involve head impact, neck load, and collision risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Follow age guidance, teach timing and landing, limit unnecessary heading volume, and stop for symptoms.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Dives, posts, rebounds, and crowded boxes create shoulder, wrist, hip, and head-contact risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Teach fall mechanics, safe service, claim/punch/stay decision rules, and crowded-box progressions.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Late, uncontrolled, two-footed, or excessive-force challenges are safety and law risks.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Teach delay, tackle timing, lawful contact, and decision to contain instead of tackle.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Fatigue can degrade touch, tackle timing, shot choice, and landing mechanics.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Separate conditioning stress from new technical learning when quality collapses.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Growth spurts can temporarily reduce coordination and increase sensitivity to kicking, sprinting, and jumping volume.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use flexible progressions, lower volume spikes, and emphasize movement quality.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Congested fixtures and premature return can combine high speed, contact, and fatigue before tissue capacity is restored.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Stage return-to-run, return-to-sprint, return-to-kick, return-to-contact, and return-to-play.

training_implications.implication: Beginners need many touches, simple rules, direction, goals, and small games rather than long isolated explanations.
training_implications.practice_design: Use ball-each warm-ups, partner passing, gates, 1v1 channels, 2v2/3v3 games, and frequent success constraints.

training_implications.implication: Intermediate work should preserve technique while adding defender cues, support angles, role responsibilities, and transition.
training_implications.practice_design: Use rondos, positional games, directional small-sided games, and phase-specific constraints.

training_implications.implication: Advanced players should train the details they will face in their position, team game model, opponent plan, and match state.
training_implications.practice_design: Use unit work, 8v8 to 11v11 phase play, scout-team behaviors, video-tagged review, and KPI feedback.

training_implications.implication: A drill should usually become more representative before simply becoming faster, longer, or more fatiguing.
training_implications.practice_design: Add pressure, direction, transition, and score before adding maximal volume.

training_implications.implication: Backend assessments should weight live success, decision rationale, and next-action outcome above isolated technique alone.
training_implications.practice_design: Use drill success plus small-sided or match clip evidence.

training_implications.implication: Line-breaking passes, 1v1 dribbles, shots, crosses, presses, and goalkeeper build-up actions are advanced only if the benefit justifies the risk.
training_implications.practice_design: Track success, turnover location, counterattack exposure, and chance quality.

training_implications.implication: Goalkeepers should not train only isolated saves; they must be included in build-up, defending space, communication, and transition.
training_implications.practice_design: Add goalkeeper roles to rondos, phase play, finishing, crossing, and defensive-line games.

training_implications.implication: Rules should be taught where they affect action: offside runs, goalkeeper handling, fouls, cards, restarts, throw-ins, penalties, and set pieces.
training_implications.practice_design: Use law-triggered constraints during realistic games rather than separate quiz-only instruction.

training_implications.implication: Long passing, shooting, crossing, clearances, and heading need volume management, especially for youth or returning players.
training_implications.practice_design: Limit high-force repetitions, rotate sides, use technical submaximal work, and track soreness.

training_implications.implication: Conditioning should reflect role demands: wide repeated sprints, midfield repeated accelerations, center-back aerial and recovery sprint load, striker high-intensity finishing runs, goalkeeper explosive lateral work.
training_implications.practice_design: Use position-specific exposure after common movement foundations are stable.

training_implications.implication: When pain, decision quality, legal safety, or tactical transfer drops, the backend should step down task complexity instead of pushing the planned level.
training_implications.practice_design: Increase space, remove live defender, lower speed, reduce volume, or return to smaller target demands.

Mastering ball control
Wave 1: Ball Mastery, First Touch, Passing Draft

skill_prerequisites: pain-free walking, jogging, stopping, and turning
can balance briefly on each foot
can make basic contact with inside, sole, and laces
understands simple stop, go, and space commands
expectations: keep the ball close while walking or slow jogging
use both feet for simple touches
stop and start without falling or losing the ball far away
look up briefly before changing direction
protect the ball from light passive pressure
typical_drills: ball-each free dribble with color or number calls
sole stop, pull, and turn gates
1v1 keep-ball in a large square with passive defender
avoid_until_ready_gates: do not teach long skill move chains before simple control survives movement
do not punish creativity when the ball stays safe
do not use tight-contact duels before balance and stopping are safe
assessment_signals: player can keep ball within two steps during a 20 meter slow dribble
uses both feet without constant prompting
can stop ball on command and restart in a new direction
eyes lift from ball at least once before a decision

all_outfield: train broad touch confidence before assigning position-only technical work
goalkeeper: include foot receiving and inside-foot passing as part of distribution foundation

skill_prerequisites: basic close control at jogging speed
can stop, turn, and restart safely
can protect the ball with body shape
understands when space is open or crowded
expectations: change direction and pace with inside, outside, and sole surfaces
use weak foot in realistic constraints
scan before entering traffic
escape pressure with a first or second touch
carry ball into open space without overdribbling
typical_drills: rondo escape touch into a gate
avoid_until_ready_gates: do not add high-speed cuts if braking alignment collapses
do not require weak-foot-only play so long that decisions become unrealistic
do not progress to tight-contact duels if the player cannot protect with body between defender and ball
assessment_signals: successful turns under light pressure
weak-foot touches are functional enough to escape or pass
ball loss rate decreases in traffic games
player accelerates after escape touch

center_back: open body to carry away from first line of pressure
fullback_wingback: carry down line and inside while scanning winger and midfielder
midfielder: use body shape to receive, protect, and escape central pressure
winger_forward: link ball mastery to 1v1 isolation and end product

skill_prerequisites: control survives live pressure and contact
two-footed touch library supports position role
can scan before and during carry
deceleration and reacceleration quality remain stable
expectations: use disguise, feint, and body shape to manipulate defenders
control ball in tight areas while protecting from contact
change rhythm to break pressure or draw an opponent
choose carry, pass, dribble, or reset by game context
retain ball quality under fatigue and match speed
typical_drills: opposed tight-space rondo with escape gate
3v3 plus neutrals in congested central zone
carry to commit defender then release
video-tagged control actions from match clips
avoid_until_ready_gates: do not reward unnecessary skill moves that slow team attack
do not overload change-of-direction volume when groin, ankle, or knee quality declines
do not progress to advanced manipulation if simple pass/carry decision is poor
assessment_signals: retains possession under live pressure
uses disguise with clear tactical effect
escape touches lead to forward action or secure reset
low turnover rate in central or defensive-third pressure

center_back: carry through first press only when cover and passing lanes support it
defensive_midfielder: receive on half-turn, protect, and escape to switch or progress
attacking_midfielder: tight-space manipulation to create line-breaking pass or shot
winger_wide_forward: 1v1 disguise linked to cutback, cross, or shot
striker_false_nine: back-to-goal protection, roll, layoff, and turn choices

source_ref_titles: Passing and receiving
Technical: Using a first touch to evade pressure
Passing circuit: Receiving between the lines
Karl Aksum on scanning
Wave 1: Ball Mastery, First Touch, Passing Draft

skill_prerequisites: can cushion a rolling ball with inside foot
can pass back to a large target
understands open body versus closed body in simple terms
can look away from ball briefly without panic
expectations: first touch stays close enough for second touch
receive with both feet from simple angles
look before receiving when time allows
receive and pass to a visible support player
use body between ball and light pressure
typical_drills: receive through a gate then pass
coach shows color before pass arrives
receive and turn to mini goal
avoid_until_ready_gates: do not demand one-touch play before two-touch control is stable
do not overcoach back-foot receiving when pressure makes front-foot protection safer
do not progress to blind turns before scan habits are visible
assessment_signals: first touch is playable on most controlled passes
player can call target before or as ball arrives
receives with inside of both feet
turnovers after first touch are decreasing

all_outfield: learn first touch to control, protect, pass, and turn
goalkeeper: receive back pass across body and play safe outlet with both feet

skill_prerequisites: two-touch control is stable
can scan before receiving in drills
understands pressure side and safe foot
can receive from different pass speeds
expectations: receive across body when forward play is available
use front-foot or outside-foot escape when pressure blocks back foot
check away and arrive to receive

typical_drills: rondo with scan or shoulder-check scoring
receive across body into target gate
check away, receive, and play forward
avoid_until_ready_gates: do not allow one-touch constraints to reward blind turnovers
do not label every front-foot touch as wrong
do not progress to tight between-lines receiving if player stands marked and static
assessment_signals: scan-to-action rate improves

player selects back foot, front foot, or set pass from pressure cue
progressive action after receiving increases

center_back: receive from goalkeeper while open to both sides and aware of pressing striker
fullback_wingback: receive on touchline with body shape to play inside, down line, or back
midfielder: receive between lines and escape central pressure
winger_wide_forward: receive wide to attack defender or combine inside

skill_prerequisites: scan habits transfer to live play

can receive aerial, bouncing, fast, or disguised passes
understands team positional spacing
expectations: receive between lines with disguise and pressure awareness
use no-touch, first-time, set, or roll actions when context demands

typical_drills: between-lines positional game with live defenders

one-touch, no-touch, or turn decision game
match-clip review of pre-receive scans and first touch
avoid_until_ready_gates: do not use advanced disguise if it delays obvious forward action
do not overload central receiving if turnover creates repeated counterattack exposure
do not progress aerial receiving volume when neck, trunk, or contact safety is poor
assessment_signals: receives under match pressure and keeps team advantage
